policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'and he stood upon the sand of the sea' is third person, rendering ἐστάθη. The chapter's own note, 'Some ancient authorities read I stood', records ἐστάθην as the reading the ASV did not adopt.
ASV plural 'names of blasphemy' renders ὀνόματα; the singular ὄνομα would be 'a name'.
ὡς and ὡσεὶ both yield ASV 'as though'; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'wondered' renders either the passive ἐθαυμάσθη or the active ἐθαύμασεν; voice is not recoverable here.
ASV 'the whole earth wondered' makes ὅλη ἡ γῆ the subject; ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ γῇ would be adverbial.
ASV 'because he gave his authority' is a causal clause with a finite verb, excluding the dative participle τῷ δεδωκότι.
ASV 'who is able to war' renders the verb δύναται and the adjective δύνατος alike.
ASV plural 'blasphemies' renders βλασφημίας.
ASV 'authority to continue forty and two months' has no object 'war'; πόλεμον is absent.

ASV 'forty and two' is not evidence for καί: the verse-18 number ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ, which has no καί, is likewise written 'Six hundred and sixty and six'. The τεσσεράκοντα/τεσσαράκοντα difference is orthographic.
ASV 'his mouth for blasphemies' is plural, rendering βλασφημίας.
ASV 'worship him' does not distinguish accusative αὐτόν from dative αὐτῷ.
English 'whose' is number-neutral, so οὗ and ὧν are equally compatible with ASV 'every one whose name'.
The resumptive αὐτοῦ is not separately rendered: 'whose name' reads the same with or without it.

ASV 'If any man is for captivity, into captivity he goeth' reflects the doubled εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν, excluding Treg's single phrase and RP's ἔχει αἰχμαλωσίαν. The two remaining readings differ only in punctuation, which the alignment cannot distinguish, and the ASV's own note calls this verse's Greek uncertain.

ASV 'if any man shall kill with the sword' is an active future rendering ἀποκτενεῖ, and 'must he be killed' renders the δεῖ of the same reading; the base ἀποκτανθῆναι would give a passive protasis. The ASV italicizes what it supplies -- 'If any man *is* for captivity' earlier in the verse -- and 'shall kill' is not italicized.
ASV present 'he maketh the earth ... to worship' renders ποιεῖ; the imperfect ἐποίει would be 'he was making'.
ASV renders the ἵνα clause with an infinitive, 'to worship', distinguishing neither the future indicative nor the aorist subjunctive.
The readings differ in the order of ἵνα, καί and πῦρ, which ASV 'that he should even make fire' does not recover.
ASV 'make fire to come down' renders the infinitive καταβαίνειν as the complement of ποιῇ; καταβαίνῃ would give a second subjunctive.
ASV 'them that dwell on the earth' has no possessive; RP's ἐμούς would add 'my'.
ASV 'the beast who hath the stroke' is present and masculine, rendering ὃς ἔχει; ὃ εἶχεν would be neuter and imperfect.
ASV 'the stroke of the sword and lived' follows τῆς μαχαίρης καὶ ἔζησεν; RP reverses the clauses.
ASV 'it was given unto him' is masculine, rendering αὐτῷ of the second beast; the feminine αὐτῇ would refer to the image.
The readings differ only in the order of δοῦναι and πνεῦμα, which ASV 'to give breath' does not recover.
ASV 'that the image of the beast should both speak' renders ἵνα, which RP omits.
ASV renders the clause passively, 'that there be given them a mark', distinguishing neither subjunctive form.
ASV singular 'a mark on their right hand' renders χάραγμα; χαράγματα would be plural.
ASV 'that no man should be able' renders δύνηται and the irregular indicative δύναται alike after ἵνα μή.

ASV 'his number is Six hundred and sixty and six' leaves 'is' unitalicized, where the ASV italicizes what it supplies -- 'If any man *is* for captivity' in verse 10. An unmarked copula indicates the translators read ἐστίν rather than supplying it.
The masculine and neuter forms differ only in agreement, and a translator reading the numeral χξϛ΄ would still spell the number out; ASV 'Six hundred and sixty and six' is compatible with all three.
